lines.text: She's twenty centimetres long. He's two point eight.
Above her mouth hangs a glowing lure. He has no lure — and no light at all.
In some deep-sea anglerfish, when he finds her, he latches on. And he never lets go.
Over time, his body fuses into hers. Their blood supply joins up.
He becomes a permanent part of her — for the rest of both their lives.
Two animals. One bloodstream. One lure.
And that lure — the light she fishes with? It isn't even hers.
Whose light it is, and seven more ways to live in the dark, is linked right here.
